meaning: A language model that reads and writes files and runs commands, here put in charge of improving a robot's policy.
The software that drives a language model as a coding agent, such as Codex or Claude Code; the same model behaves differently under different agent programs.
A helper agent that a coding agent starts to study one line of work in parallel.
A 2026 research system from NVIDIA and two universities that gives each of eight real robot stations its own coding agent, which improves the policy against a frozen success check.
In ENPIRE, two robot arms, three cameras, one workstation with one GPU and one coding agent; the fleet has eight.
One attempt at the task, from a reset until the policy succeeds, fails or runs out of time; section 16 also calls it an episode or a rollout.
In ENPIRE's headline score, one reset followed by up to eight attempts, each made after seeing the previous failure.
The share of rollouts with a success within k attempts; pass@1 is the first-try rate and pass@8 a measure of recovery.
Drawing N independent attempts and counting a success if any succeeds; ENPIRE's retries are not independent because each follows a seen failure.
Code that returns pass or fail for one trial; its verdict is the grade the agent works to raise. In ENPIRE the agent writes it once with a person and it is then frozen.
The routine that puts the scene back so the next trial can start; whoever controls it chooses the test.
Built once before the loop starts and from then on only read by the agent: the verifier, the reset and the safety limits.
Of the trials a check passes, the share that truly succeeded; the bar that keeps false passes, which an optimising agent can chase, out of the grade.
Of the trials that truly succeeded, the share a check passes.
The average of a detector's accuracy on successes and on failures; 0.5 is chance.
SEAR's grading rule: a separate process that receives the frozen policy, holds the start states and grading code, and ignores any success the policy claims.
A 2026 benchmark that runs coding agents on simulated and real robot tasks and grades them with a sealed judge.

expansion: Agentic Skill Programming through Iterative Robot Exploration
meaning: A 2026 loop in which coding agents write robot control programs, train no weights, and keep verified repairs as text skills.
A 2026 single-author preview preprint in which a language-model controller owns measurement and the keep-or-discard decision, with a statistical gate on promotion.
A 2026 loop that does the agent's trial and error in simulation before spending a few real-robot trials.
A 2026 loop in which a coding agent first rewrites the instructions, tools and procedure around a frozen VLA, then fine-tunes only unreliable sub-steps; tested on the SO-101.
A large pretrained policy that maps camera images and an instruction to robot actions (section 5).
Conditions the training demonstrations did not show, such as new objects, sizes or orientations.
The range of true success rates that could plausibly have produced an observed count (section 16); with every trial a success its lower end is n / (n + z^2).
Training a policy to imitate recorded demonstrations (section 4).
Improving a policy from its own scored trials instead of from demonstrations (section 8).
The share of research wall-clock time during which the robot is running an experiment.
The share of research wall-clock time during which the station's GPU is in use.
Context a language-model provider has already processed on an earlier call and reads again; about 96% of an ENPIRE agent's tokens.
The whole run of ideas toward the goal, which can outlast one agent session.
One more user submitting jobs to shared hardware; an agent is one that asks for a GPU in bursts and consumes tokens steadily.
AWS's managed job queue: it runs each job in a container on instances it starts.
The AWS Batch job timeout; a job has none unless it is set, in the job definition or at submission.
One AWS Batch submission that fans out into many copies; the children inherit the parent's timeout.
The most vCPUs an AWS Batch compute environment may run at once; it caps GPUs only through the instance types allowed.
The node autoscaler for Kubernetes on EKS; a NodePool's spec.limits can cap GPUs by name, checked eventually, so a fast burst can overrun it.
A Karpenter object that describes which nodes may be launched and, through spec.limits, how many resources in total.
An AWS Batch policy that divides a shared queue among teams or agents by weight; it divides capacity in proportion and is not a GPU-hour budget.
An AWS Batch counted resource, such as a licence token, that a job waits for; one robot station can be modelled as a count of one.
An AWS feature, announced 9 November 2026, that runs a pod, task or workload in its own Firecracker microVM with its own kernel; CPU only, no GPU passthrough.
A lightweight virtual machine; Nitro Sandboxes use the Firecracker microVM.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, AWS's managed host for agents; a session on its microVMs ends after at most 8 hours.
AWS's managed Kubernetes.
